title: How lifts (elevators) work
examples: How does the lift know when to stop exactly?
What is the difference between the motor and the cables?
Why do they use a counterweight in the lift?

explain.say: Today we will learn how lifts move people up and down.
First we look at the cables that connect the lift car.

items: Lifting Car: The box you ride in
Cables: Strong steel wires attached to the car

draw.text: Cables: Connect car to machine room

explain.say: Next we learn about pulleys which help change the direction of force.

items: Pulley Wheel: The large rotating wheel

explain.say: The counterweight balances the lift car to save energy.
The motor provides the power to pull the entire system up or down.

items: Motor Housing: Contains the motor parts

explain.say: A real life example is using a large crane on a building site.

faq.q: Why is the counterweight so important for the lift?
faq.a: The counterweight helps balance the lift car's weight. This means the motor does not have to work as hard to move the lift. It makes the whole system run more efficiently.
asks: Does the counterweight make it faster?

faq.q: What happens if the cables break?
faq.a: The lift has safety brakes that automatically engage. These brakes stop the car immediately to prevent it from falling. This is a critical safety feature.
asks: How do lifts stop if they fail?
Are lifts safe if the cables snap?
What stops the lift if it goes too fast?

faq.q: Is the motor always connected to the car?
faq.a: No, the motor is usually connected to the main winding drum, not directly to the car. It pulls the cables, and the car moves along the cables. This setup is much more powerful.
asks: Where is the motor in a big lift?
Does the motor pull the car directly?

faq.q: Do all lifts use the same system?
faq.a: No, older lifts might use different systems. Modern lifts use complex electric motors, cables, and counterweights for efficiency and safety. The basic principles remain the same.
asks: Are all elevators built the same way?
What makes a modern lift different?
What are the main parts of a lift?

faq.q: How does the lift know which floor to stop at?
faq.a: The lift has sensors and control panels that know the exact floor numbers. When you press a button, it sends a signal to the control system. The system then stops the motor precisely at that floor level.
asks: How does the lift stop perfectly?
What tells the lift where to go?
Does the lift use a computer?

facts: Lifts use strong steel cables for support.
The counterweight helps balance the load, saving motor power.
Safety brakes engage automatically if the lift moves too fast.
The motor provides the rotational force to lift the car.

quiz.say: What component balances the weight of the lift car?
quiz.why: The counterweight is specifically designed to balance the car's weight, making the motor's job easier.

wrong.0: Safety brakes only stop the lift; they do not help with the normal lifting balance.
wrong.1: The motor provides power, but it is the counterweight that provides the balance.
wrong.2: Cables are the connection, but the counterweight is the object used for balancing.

quiz.say: If the lift is carrying many people, what system helps manage the extra force needed?
quiz.why: A heavier load means more force, and the counterweight helps offset some of that extra force.

wrong.0: Pulleys change direction, but they do not reduce the overall weight difference.
wrong.1: Safety brakes are for emergencies, not for managing normal changes in load.
wrong.3: The motor will work harder, but the counterweight reduces how much harder it needs to work.

quiz.say: Which part generates the actual power to move the lift?
quiz.why: The motor is the machine that converts electrical energy into the mechanical force needed for movement.

wrong.0: Cables only transmit the force; they do not create the force themselves.
wrong.1: The counterweight is a mass used for balancing, not for generating power.
wrong.2: Pulleys are mechanical guides; they direct the force but do not create it.
